title: 1 · Sounds, silent letters and liaison
blurb: Read French words aloud: the vowels, the nasal sounds, the silent letters, and the links between words.

title: 2 · Greetings: tu and vous
blurb: Greet people at any time of day, say please and thank you, and choose between tu and vous.

title: 3 · Gender and articles: le, la, l', les, un, une, des
blurb: Name things around the house with the right word for "the" and "a", in the singular and the plural.

title: 4 · être and avoir: I am, I have
blurb: Say who you are and what you have with être and avoir, and use avoir for age, hunger and feeling cold.

title: 5 · Subject and stress pronouns: je, moi, on
blurb: Say "me", "with you" and "and you?" with moi and toi, and use on, the everyday "we".

title: 6 · Adjectives: agreement and place
blurb: Describe clothes and things with colors and sizes, putting each adjective in the right place and the right form.

title: 7 · Present tense: -er verbs
blurb: Talk about work, school and daily life with regular -er verbs, giving each subject its own ending.

title: 8 · ne … pas
blurb: Say what you are not, don't have and don't do, with ne … pas around the verb and pas de.

title: 9 · Questions: est-ce que, qui, où
blurb: Ask yes/no questions and questions with where, when, why and which, without any word for "do".

title: 10 · c'est and il y a
blurb: Point things out with c'est, describe people with il est and elle est, and say what there is in town with il y a.

title: 11 · mon / ma / mes, ce / cette / ces
blurb: Say my, your, his, her, our and their, and point at this or that, with the right form for each noun.

title: 12 · Numbers, time and dates
blurb: Count to 1,000, tell the time, read prices in euros and give a date.

title: 13 · du, de la, des: some
blurb: Ask for and talk about an amount of food or drink with du, de la, de l' and des.

title: 14 · je voudrais: polite requests
blurb: Order at a café or bakery and ask staff and strangers for things politely.

title: 15 · Prepositions of place and time
blurb: Say where you are, where you're going and when, with à, au, en, chez and other small words.

title: 16 · aller, faire, venir, prendre
blurb: Use four everyday irregular verbs to say where you go, what you do, where you're from and what you take, and talk about the weather.

title: 17 · vouloir, pouvoir, devoir + infinitive
blurb: Say what you want to do, can do and have to do, ask for help, and say what you know how to do.

title: 18 · Futur proche: je vais + verb
blurb: Talk about your plans with aller + a verb, and say when they will happen.

title: 19 · Reflexive verbs
blurb: Describe your daily routine with reflexive verbs like se lever and s'appeler.

title: 20 · Imperative and il faut
blurb: Give and follow instructions (Tourne, Tournez, Allons-y) and say what has to be done with il faut.

title: 21 · Passé composé with avoir and être
blurb: Say what you did: j'ai mangé, je suis allé(e), with the right helper verb and agreement.

title: 22 · et, ou, mais, alors
blurb: Join your sentences with and, or, but, so, because, then and when, and never mix up ou and où.

title: 23 · Spoken French: what you'll hear
blurb: Recognize everyday spoken French: ne dropped, on for 'we', t'as, y a and questions with no question word.

title: 24 · Imparfait vs passé composé
blurb: Describe the past (the weather, how things were, what you used to do) and set it against what happened.

title: 25 · Futur simple
blurb: Talk about the future in one word (je travaillerai, je serai) and use the future after quand.

title: 26 · Pronouns le, lui, en, y
blurb: Say 'I'll take it', 'I'm calling her', 'I'd like two' and 'I'm going there' with the pronoun in the right place.

title: 27 · Comparing: plus, moins, le plus
blurb: Compare people and things (taller than, as nice as, the best) with the adjective still agreeing.

title: 28 · qui, que, où
blurb: Build longer descriptions (the friend who lives in Lyon, the movie I saw, the town where I live) without dropping a word.
